summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for his 16th cycle of maintenance high-dose methotrexate and rituximab. He reported stable health but noted a recurrence of visual floaters. He tolerated the chemotherapy well, with no acute neurological deterioration. Methotrexate was administered with aggressive hydration and urinary alkalinization to prevent renal toxicity, and leucovorin rescue was continued until levels dropped below 0.2 µM. MRI of the brain and CT of the torso showed no evidence of lymphoma recurrence. He developed mild headache and nausea on the day of discharge, which were managed with Midrin and antiemetics. His home aspirin was held during admission due to potential interaction and safely restarted at discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up scheduled in four months.
problems: Hodgkin's disease, mixed cellularity, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Family history of ischemic heart disease
